title: Comparing
description: Compare people and things with plus, moins, aussi, meilleur and mieux, and say the most or the least.
rule: With an adjective, use plus (more), moins (less) or aussi (as) + adjective + que, and the adjective still agrees: Marie est plus grande que Paul. With a noun, use plus de, moins de or autant de + noun + que (j’ai plus de livres que toi); after a verb, use plus, moins or autant + que (il travaille plus que moi). Bon becomes meilleur, which agrees like an adjective (une meilleure idée), and bien becomes mieux, which goes with a verb (elle chante mieux); never say plus bon or plus bien. The superlative is le, la or les + plus or moins + adjective, and the group it belongs to follows with de: le plus grand de la classe, la meilleure de l’équipe. Adjectives that follow the noun also follow it in the superlative, with the article repeated (le film le plus intéressant); adjectives that go before the noun can take either order (la plus belle ville or la ville la plus belle). After que, use a stressed pronoun: que moi, que toi, que lui, qu’elle.
example: Paul est plus grand que Marie. · Elle chante mieux que moi. · C’est le film le plus intéressant de l’année.
aside: Moins bon and aussi bon are correct; only plus bon becomes meilleur. Likewise moins bien and aussi bien are correct; only plus bien becomes mieux.

exercises.source: Marie est plus ____ que son frère.
answers: grande
exercises.feedback: The adjective still agrees in a comparison.
exercises.explanation: The adjective agrees with Marie, the first person: plus grande.

exercises.source: Le train est ____ rapide que le bus.
answers: plus
exercises.feedback: With an adjective, there is no de.
exercises.explanation: Before an adjective, more is plus: plus rapide que.

exercises.instruction: Write the word for as (as … as).
exercises.source: Ma sœur est ____ sportive que moi.
answers: aussi
exercises.feedback: With an adjective, as … as is not autant.
exercises.explanation: Before an adjective, as … as is aussi … que: aussi sportive que moi.

exercises.source: Ce film est ____ intéressant que le livre.
answers: moins
exercises.hint: You need the opposite of plus.
exercises.feedback: There is no de before an adjective.
exercises.explanation: Before an adjective, less is moins: moins intéressant que.

exercises.source: Paul is taller than Marie.
answers: Paul est plus grand que Marie.
exercises.feedback: Use the pattern plus + adjective + que.
exercises.explanation: Taller than is plus grand que, with grand agreeing with Paul.

exercises.instruction: Join the two sentences with aussi … que.
exercises.source: Léa est grande. Sa mère est grande aussi.
answers: Léa est aussi grande que sa mère.
Sa mère est aussi grande que Léa.
exercises.feedback: Put the comparison word before the adjective and que after it.
exercises.explanation: Equal qualities take aussi + adjective + que: aussi grande que sa mère.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: She is more patient than him. Leave one tile unused.
exercises.source: She is more patient than him.
answers: Elle est plus patiente que lui.
exercises.hint: After que, use a stressed pronoun.
exercises.feedback: Check the pronoun after que.
exercises.explanation: The pattern is plus + adjective + que, and after que the pronoun is lui, not il.

exercises.source: Ma maison est plus petit que ta maison.
answers: Ma maison est plus petite que ta maison.
exercises.feedback: The adjective still has to agree.
exercises.explanation: Petite agrees with the feminine noun maison, even in a comparison.

exercises.source: J’ai ____ livres que toi.
answers: plus de
exercises.feedback: Before a noun, you need a small extra word.
exercises.explanation: Before a noun, more is plus de, and de does not change: plus de livres.

exercises.source: Il boit ____ café que moi.
answers: autant de
exercises.feedback: Aussi goes with adjectives, not nouns.
exercises.explanation: Before a noun, as much is autant de: autant de café.

exercises.source: Nous avons ____ temps que vous.
answers: moins de
exercises.feedback: Before a noun you need two words.
exercises.explanation: Before a noun, less is moins de: moins de temps.

exercises.instruction: Write the words for as many.
exercises.source: Elle a ____ cousins que sa sœur.
answers: autant de
exercises.feedback: Aussi does not go with nouns.
exercises.explanation: Before a noun, as many is autant de: autant de cousins.

exercises.source: I have more work than you (to a friend).
answers: J’ai plus de travail que toi.
J’ai davantage de travail que toi.
exercises.feedback: Check the word after plus and the pronoun after que.
exercises.explanation: Before a noun, more is plus de, and after que the pronoun is toi: plus de travail que toi.

exercises.source: Tom has fewer brothers than Julie.
answers: Tom a moins de frères que Julie.
exercises.feedback: Before a noun, add a small word after moins.
exercises.explanation: Before a noun, fewer is moins de: moins de frères.

exercises.source: Paris a plus des habitants que Lyon.
answers: Paris a plus d’habitants que Lyon.
exercises.hint: After plus, the small word never changes to des.
exercises.feedback: Look at the word after plus, and remember elision.
exercises.explanation: The pattern is plus de + noun, and de becomes d’ before a vowel or silent h: plus d’habitants.

exercises.instruction: Join the two sentences with autant de … que.
exercises.source: Paul a trois chats. Marc a trois chats aussi.
answers: Paul a autant de chats que Marc.
Marc a autant de chats que Paul.
exercises.feedback: Use the pattern for equal quantities of a noun.
exercises.explanation: Equal quantities of a noun take autant de + noun + que: autant de chats que Marc.

exercises.source: Il travaille ____ que moi.
answers: plus
exercises.hint: You are comparing an action, not a thing.
exercises.feedback: After a verb, no de is needed.
exercises.explanation: After a verb, more is simply plus: il travaille plus que moi.

exercises.source: Tu dors ____ que ton frère.
answers: autant
exercises.feedback: Aussi goes with adjectives; after a verb, as much is different.
exercises.explanation: After a verb, as much is autant: tu dors autant que ton frère.

exercises.source: Je sors ____ qu’avant.
answers: moins
exercises.feedback: After a verb, no de is needed.
exercises.explanation: After a verb, less is moins: je sors moins qu’avant.

exercises.source: She reads more than me.
answers: Elle lit plus que moi.
Elle lit davantage que moi.
exercises.feedback: Check the word after the verb and the pronoun after que.
exercises.explanation: After a verb, more is plus, and after que the pronoun is moi: elle lit plus que moi.

exercises.source: We eat as much as you (you, plural).
answers: Nous mangeons autant que vous.
On mange autant que vous.
exercises.feedback: After a verb, as much is not aussi.
exercises.explanation: After a verb, as much as is autant que: nous mangeons autant que vous.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: He works less than her. Leave the extra tiles unused.
exercises.source: He works less than her.
answers: Il travaille moins qu’elle.
exercises.hint: After a verb, no de is needed.
exercises.feedback: Check the words after moins.
exercises.explanation: After a verb, less than is moins que, and que becomes qu’ before elle.

exercises.source: Mon frère mange plus de moi.
answers: Mon frère mange plus que moi.
exercises.hint: Moi is a person, not a quantity.
exercises.feedback: The word before moi is wrong.
exercises.explanation: After a verb, the comparison is plus que: il mange plus que moi. De is only for a noun after plus.

exercises.source: Ce gâteau est ____ que l’autre.
answers: meilleur
exercises.hint: Better here describes gâteau, a masculine noun.
exercises.feedback: Bon has a special comparative form.
exercises.explanation: Better describing a masculine noun is meilleur: ce gâteau est meilleur.

exercises.source: Elle chante ____ que moi.
answers: mieux
exercises.hint: Better here describes how she sings.
exercises.feedback: Bien has a special comparative form.
exercises.explanation: Better describing a verb is mieux: elle chante mieux que moi.

exercises.source: C’est une ____ idée.
answers: meilleure
exercises.hint: Better here describes idée, a feminine noun.
exercises.feedback: This word agrees like an adjective.
exercises.explanation: Better describing a noun is meilleur, and it agrees with the feminine idée: une meilleure idée.

exercises.instruction: Write meilleur or mieux, in the right form.
exercises.source: Tu nages ____ que l’année dernière.
answers: mieux
exercises.hint: Better here describes how you swim.
exercises.feedback: This describes an action, not a thing.
exercises.explanation: Better describing a verb is mieux, which never changes: tu nages mieux.

exercises.instruction: Write meilleur or mieux, in the right form.
exercises.source: Ces pommes sont ____ que les autres.
answers: meilleures
exercises.hint: Better here describes pommes, a feminine plural noun.
exercises.feedback: This word agrees like an adjective.
exercises.explanation: Better describing a noun is meilleur, and it agrees with pommes: meilleures.

exercises.source: Ce restaurant est plus bon que l’autre.
answers: Ce restaurant est meilleur que l’autre.
exercises.feedback: Bon has a special comparative form.
exercises.explanation: The comparative of bon is meilleur: ce restaurant est meilleur que l’autre.

exercises.source: Il joue plus bien que son père.
answers: Il joue mieux que son père.
exercises.feedback: Bien has a special comparative form.
exercises.explanation: The comparative of bien is mieux: il joue mieux que son père.

exercises.source: My sister cooks better than me.
answers: Ma sœur cuisine mieux que moi.
Ma sœur fait mieux la cuisine que moi.
exercises.feedback: This describes an action, and check the pronoun after que.
exercises.explanation: Better describing a verb is mieux, and after que the pronoun is moi.

exercises.source: C’est le plus grand élève ____ la classe.
answers: de
exercises.hint: In the class is part of a superlative.
exercises.feedback: After a superlative, French does not use que or à for the group.
exercises.explanation: After a superlative, the group is introduced with de: le plus grand élève de la classe.

exercises.source: Julie est ____ plus rapide de l’équipe.
answers: la
exercises.feedback: The article agrees too.
exercises.explanation: The article in a superlative agrees with the person: Julie est la plus rapide.

exercises.source: Ce sont ____ plus beaux jours de l’année.
answers: les
exercises.feedback: The article agrees with the noun.
exercises.explanation: Jours is plural, so the superlative takes les: les plus beaux jours.

exercises.instruction: Write the words for the best.
exercises.source: C’est ____ restaurant du quartier.
answers: le meilleur
exercises.hint: Restaurant is masculine, and bon has a special form.
exercises.feedback: Never say le plus bon.
exercises.explanation: The superlative of bon is le meilleur: le meilleur restaurant du quartier.

exercises.source: Emma is the youngest in the family.
answers: Emma est la plus jeune de la famille.
exercises.hint: In the family is part of a superlative.
exercises.feedback: Check the article and the word before la famille.
exercises.explanation: The superlative is la plus jeune, and the group takes de: de la famille.

exercises.source: It’s the best film of the year.
answers: C’est le meilleur film de l’année.
exercises.hint: Best is the superlative of bon.
exercises.feedback: Never say le plus bon.
exercises.explanation: The best is le meilleur, and the group takes de: de l’année.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite it as a superlative: Léo is the most serious in the class.
exercises.source: Léo est plus sérieux que Tom.
answers: Léo est le plus sérieux de la classe.
exercises.hint: Add an article, and use de for the group.
exercises.feedback: A superlative needs an article and de, not que.
exercises.explanation: The superlative adds le before plus and introduces the group with de: le plus sérieux de la classe.

exercises.source: Marie est la plus bonne de l’équipe.
answers: Marie est la meilleure de l’équipe.
exercises.feedback: Bon has a special form in the superlative too.
exercises.explanation: The superlative of bon is le meilleur, here la meilleure for Marie.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: She is the least tired in the group. Leave the extra tiles unused.
exercises.source: She is the least tired in the group.
answers: Elle est la moins fatiguée du groupe.
exercises.feedback: Check the article and the word for in the.
exercises.explanation: The superlative is la moins fatiguée, and the group takes de: du groupe.

exercises.source: C’est ____ de l’année.
answers: le film le plus intéressant
exercises.feedback: Keep intéressant after the noun and repeat the article.
exercises.explanation: Adjectives that follow the noun keep that place in the superlative, with the article repeated: le film le plus intéressant.

exercises.source: Voici ____ de Paris.
answers: le restaurant le moins cher
exercises.hint: Cher meaning expensive follows the noun.
exercises.feedback: Keep cher after the noun and repeat the article.
exercises.explanation: Cher follows the noun, so the superlative follows too, with the article repeated: le restaurant le moins cher.

exercises.source: Lyon is the most beautiful city in France.
answers: Lyon est la plus belle ville de France.
Lyon est la ville la plus belle de France.
exercises.hint: Beau can go before the noun.
exercises.feedback: Check the article and the word before France.
exercises.explanation: Belle can go before the noun (la plus belle ville) or after it with the article repeated (la ville la plus belle).

exercises.source: It’s the most interesting book in the library.
answers: C’est le livre le plus intéressant de la bibliothèque.
exercises.feedback: Keep the adjective after the noun and repeat the article.
exercises.explanation: Intéressant follows the noun, so the superlative does too: le livre le plus intéressant.

exercises.instruction: Make it the most expensive dress with plus, keeping the adjective after the noun.
exercises.source: J’ai acheté la robe chère.
answers: J’ai acheté la robe la plus chère.
exercises.feedback: After the noun, the superlative needs its own article.
exercises.explanation: Chère follows the noun, so the superlative is la robe la plus chère, with la repeated.

exercises.source: C’est la question plus difficile de l’examen.
answers: C’est la question la plus difficile de l’examen.
exercises.hint: A word is missing before plus.
exercises.feedback: After the noun, the superlative needs its own article.
exercises.explanation: Difficile follows the noun, so the article is repeated: la question la plus difficile.

exercises.instruction: Build the sentence: It’s the biggest house in the street. You may not need every tile.
exercises.source: It’s the biggest house in the street.
answers: C’est la plus grande maison de la rue.
C’est la maison la plus grande de la rue.
exercises.hint: Grand can go before the noun.
exercises.feedback: Check the article and the word before la rue.
exercises.explanation: Grande can go before the noun (la plus grande maison) or after it with the article repeated (la maison la plus grande).

exercises.instruction: Write the missing words: the quietest area in the town.
exercises.source: C’est le quartier ____ calme de la ville.
answers: le plus
exercises.feedback: After the noun, the superlative needs its own article.
exercises.explanation: Calme follows the noun, so the superlative repeats the article: le quartier le plus calme.
